why: A piece standing where nothing buries it, with nothing in its document saying that is deliberate. `prefab/gallery-yard` is an `open_top` court — paving, a plinth and four corner posts — so the air a body stands in leaves through the sky, and air that gets outside runs along every side the layout puts near it. Placed as its own area it has no neighbour, and `horizon: void` is the horizon that declares there is nothing outside the placed geometry, so it buries nothing either: four sides of the piece put blocks where a party can see them and the document answers for one, `down`. That is the shape the third page walk shipped — a cave piece authored to be inside a hill, laid on a shore, its cap left standing in the sky over the beach — and it is known from the document and the bytes before anything is placed, so `DW0886` refuses it at validation, naming the sides, the cell the party gets out through, and the moves; `DW0885` is the same question asked of the assembled world, and the build's own refusal is proven in `crates/delvec/tests/piece_exposure.rs`, where the seating answer and the build answer are held to each other on one geometry. The edit script is emptied for a reason of ORDERING and not of severity: this platform really is a walkable edge over the void, and the per-batch `DW0322` inside the stage-7 replay would otherwise be what a later stage meets. It declares no unit: `shown_faces` is prefab metadata rather than a stage schema unit, and it is bound on the site-plan point, where `gallery-yard` declares `down` and the build reports `1 `shown_faces` declaration(s) of which 1 are bound`.
